title: EEG recordings for semantic decoding of imagined animals and tools during auditory imagery task
description: This dataset comprises electroencephalography (EEG) recordings from 7 participants performing an auditory imagery task, wherein subjects imagined sounds produced by objects from semantic categories (animals and tools) for 5-second intervals. The study employs a 64-electrode BioSemi ActiveTwo system sampled at 2048 Hz, with concurrent electrooculography and physiological monitoring to support semantic decoding and brain-computer interface research.
methods_description: EEG data were acquired using a BioSemi ActiveTwo system with 64 electrodes positioned according to the international 10-20 system, plus bilateral earlobe reference electrodes. Electrooculography was recorded from four electrodes (vertical and horizontal placements around the right eye). Additional physiological measurements included wrist electrodes (left and right) and respiration monitoring via a waist belt. Sampling rate: 2048 Hz.
